quests.instruction: Which order makes the most sense for getting ready for school in the morning?
quests.correctAnswer: Wake up, get dressed, eat breakfast, put on shoes ⏰
options: Put on shoes, wake up, eat breakfast, get dressed 👟
Wake up, get dressed, eat breakfast, put on shoes ⏰
Eat breakfast, put on shoes, wake up, get dressed 🍞
quests.hint: Think about what must happen first before you can do the rest.
quests.explanation: You have to be awake before you can get ready, and shoes usually come last, just before you leave.
quests.funFact: Many people find that doing the steps in the same order each morning helps them remember every one.

quests.instruction: Bea lays out her clothes and packs her school bag the night before. How does this help her morning?
quests.correctAnswer: Her morning feels calmer and less rushed ⏱️
options: Her morning feels calmer and less rushed ⏱️
Her family can skip breakfast to save time 🍞
School will start a little later for her 🕘
quests.hint: What jobs are already finished when the alarm rings?
quests.explanation: Preparing ahead means fewer jobs and fewer things to forget when time is short.
quests.funFact: Many families find that choosing clothes and packing bags in the evening makes the next morning smoother.

quests.instruction: Teddy's family leaves home at 8:00. Breakfast takes 20 minutes, getting dressed takes 10 minutes, and packing his bag takes 5 minutes. If he does these one after another, what is the latest time he should wake up?
quests.hint: Add up the minutes first, then count backward from 8:00.
quests.explanation: 20 + 10 + 5 makes 35 minutes, and 35 minutes before 8:00 is 7:25.
quests.funFact: Counting back from the time you must leave is a good way to plan any busy morning.

quests.instruction: Mo is served a vegetable he has never tried and is not sure about. What is a polite way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: Try one small bite, then say 'no thank you' 🥄
options: Say 'yuck' loudly and push the plate away 😖
Hide it under the rice and hope no one sees 🙈
Try one small bite, then say 'no thank you' 🥄
quests.hint: Think about how to be honest without hurting the cook's feelings.
quests.explanation: Trying a little shows respect for the person who made the food. If you do not like it, you can say so politely.
quests.funFact: Children sometimes need to try a new food many times before they come to like it.

quests.instruction: Gil's cousin is allergic to peanuts and is coming for dinner. What should Gil's family do?
quests.correctAnswer: Check labels and keep peanuts out of his meal 🥜
options: Serve peanuts anyway and hope he avoids them 🙈
Tell him to eat at home before he arrives 🚪
Check labels and keep peanuts out of his meal 🥜
quests.hint: A food allergy can make someone seriously ill, so plan ahead.
quests.explanation: Food allergies can cause serious reactions. Reading labels and keeping the meal safe shows care for a guest.
quests.funFact: Peanut allergy is one of the most common food allergies in children.

quests.instruction: Dina wants the rice, which is on the far side of the table. What is a polite way to get it?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask, 'Could you please pass the rice?' 🗣️
options: Ask, 'Could you please pass the rice?' 🗣️
Stand on her chair and reach across 🪑
Grab the bowl and pull it over 🍚
quests.hint: Use your words, and remember the polite ones.
quests.explanation: Asking politely keeps the table calm and safe, and people are happy to pass the dish.
quests.funFact: Almost every language has its own way of saying 'please' and 'thank you'.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a calming bedtime routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Bath, brushing teeth, and a quiet story 📖
options: A pillow fight with loud music playing 🎶
A scary movie and a big sugary snack 🍬
Bath, brushing teeth, and a quiet story 📖
quests.hint: A good bedtime routine helps your body slow down.
quests.explanation: Calm, predictable steps tell the body that it is time to sleep. Exciting activities and sugar make it harder to wind down.
quests.funFact: Doing the same steps in the same order each night helps many children fall asleep more easily.

quests.instruction: Why do many families put screens away before bedtime?
quests.correctAnswer: Screens can make falling asleep harder 📱
options: Screens can make falling asleep harder 📱
Screens use too much electricity at night ⚡
Screens stop working after dark 🌙
quests.hint: Think about how your mind feels after a fast, bright show.
quests.explanation: Bright light and exciting shows keep the brain alert, so using screens right before bed can make sleep harder.
quests.funFact: Many sleep experts suggest turning screens off about an hour before bed.

quests.instruction: Rue cannot sleep because of a worry about tomorrow's test. What could help?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up and take slow breaths 🌬️
options: Tell a grown-up and take slow breaths 🌬️
Stay up all night trying to study more 📚
Say nothing and keep lying there awake 😟
quests.hint: Worries often feel smaller when you share them.
quests.explanation: Talking to a caring adult and slowing your breathing can help a worried mind settle.
quests.funFact: Slow, deep breathing tells the body it is safe, which can make it easier to relax.

quests.instruction: Eden finds a note from school in her bag. What should she do with it when she gets home?
quests.correctAnswer: Give it to a grown-up at home right away 📝
options: Keep it in the bag until next week 🎒
Give it to a grown-up at home right away 📝
Throw it away so it does not get lost 🗑️
quests.hint: School notes are written for the people who look after you.
quests.explanation: Notes can tell families about trips, meetings, or health matters. Handing it over quickly makes sure nothing is missed.
quests.funFact: Many schools now send messages by email or an app as well as paper notes, so families often check both.

quests.instruction: Which setup helps a child do homework well?
quests.correctAnswer: A quiet spot at a regular time 📚
options: A noisy room with the TV on 📺
A quiet spot at a regular time 📚
A different place every day 🔀
quests.hint: Think about what helps you concentrate.
quests.explanation: A regular time and a quiet place help the brain get ready to work and make it easier to start.
quests.funFact: Some studies suggest people concentrate better when their phone is in another room.

quests.instruction: After school, Una feels tired and cranky. Which routine could help her?
quests.correctAnswer: A snack and a short rest before homework 🍎
options: A snack and a short rest before homework 🍎
Homework straight away with no break ✏️
Skipping dinner to catch up 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about what a tired body needs.
quests.explanation: A snack and quiet rest give back energy so that Una can concentrate again.
quests.funFact: Short breaks help people learn better than working for hours without stopping.

quests.instruction: Dax's family has a weekly planning chat every Sunday. What is it good for?
quests.correctAnswer: Sharing the plans for the week 📅
options: Sharing the plans for the week 📅
Picking a winner for the week 🏆
Deciding who sleeps first 🌙
quests.hint: Think about what changes from week to week.
quests.explanation: A short planning chat lets everyone know where they need to be and when, and gives people a chance to ask for help.
quests.funFact: Some families pin the week's plan on the fridge so that everyone can check it.

quests.instruction: Which calendar entry is the clearest?
quests.correctAnswer: Dentist, Wednesday 4:30 pm, Isla 🦷
options: Appointment with a doctor soon ❓
Something happening midweek 📆
Dentist, Wednesday 4:30 pm, Isla 🦷
quests.hint: A clear entry says what, when, and who.
quests.explanation: A good entry says what the event is, when it happens, and who is going, so nobody has to guess.
quests.funFact: Calendars that use a different color for each person help families see who is busy when.

quests.instruction: Dax's dad has a work trip on Thursday, and Dax has football practice at 5:00. Why is it helpful to write both on the shared calendar?
quests.correctAnswer: So another adult can plan a ride 🚗
options: So another adult can plan a ride 🚗
So Dax can skip the practice 🙈
So nobody needs to talk about it 🤐
quests.hint: Think about who needs to know.
quests.explanation: When the usual driver is away, the family needs to know in advance so that they can arrange another ride.
quests.funFact: Plans are easier to follow when changes are written where everyone can see them.

quests.instruction: When is it most important to wash your hands?
quests.correctAnswer: Before eating and after the toilet 🧼
options: Only before you go to bed 🌙
Only once a day, in the morning ☀️
Before eating and after the toilet 🧼
quests.hint: Think about when germs could get from your hands into your body.
quests.explanation: Washing with soap before eating and after using the toilet removes germs that can make you sick.
quests.funFact: Health experts usually advise washing with soap for about 20 seconds.

quests.instruction: How often do dentists suggest brushing your teeth?
quests.correctAnswer: Twice a day, for about two minutes 🪥
options: Only once a week, on Sunday mornings 📅
Twice a day, for about two minutes 🪥
Only when a tooth starts to hurt 😬
quests.hint: Teeth need care every day, not only when something is wrong.
quests.explanation: Brushing morning and night for two minutes removes the plaque that causes cavities.
quests.funFact: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.

quests.instruction: Jin wakes up with a high temperature and feels very tired. What is the best plan for the day?
quests.correctAnswer: Rest at home and tell a grown-up 🛏️
options: Go to school anyway to avoid missing it 🏫
Run around to feel better 🏃
Rest at home and tell a grown-up 🛏️
quests.hint: A body that is fighting an illness needs rest and care.
quests.explanation: Resting at home helps you recover and keeps germs away from other people. A grown-up can decide whether to call a doctor.
quests.funFact: Staying home when sick helps stop illnesses from spreading to classmates.

quests.instruction: Hari's mom works at night, so Hari's family eats their main meal at lunchtime. Is that okay?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, meals can fit a family's schedule 🍽️
options: No, the main meal must always be at night 🌙
Yes, meals can fit a family's schedule 🍽️
No, all families must eat at six o'clock 🕕
quests.hint: Is there one correct time for every family to eat?
quests.explanation: Families have different work and school hours, so their routines are built around what works for them.
quests.funFact: Many people work at night, including nurses, bakers, and bus drivers.

quests.instruction: It is the school holiday, and Sol's family wakes up later than usual. Which habit would still help keep the days steady?
quests.correctAnswer: Keeping mealtimes roughly the same 🍽️
options: Having no regular mealtimes at all 🍽️
Never leaving the house 🏠
Keeping mealtimes roughly the same 🍽️
quests.hint: Which habit gives the day some structure?
quests.explanation: Even when other things change, keeping a few steady habits, such as meals, helps everyone feel settled.
quests.funFact: Many families find a loose daily rhythm easier to keep than a strict timetable in the holidays.

quests.instruction: Guests arrive, so bedtime is an hour later tonight. What is the best way to handle it?
quests.correctAnswer: Enjoy tonight, then go back to routine 🌙
options: Skip bedtime for the whole week from now 🎉
Refuse to say hello to any of the guests 🚪
Enjoy tonight, then go back to routine 🌙
quests.hint: A routine can bend without breaking.
quests.explanation: A one-off change is fine. Going back to your usual routine afterwards keeps sleep and mood steady.
quests.funFact: Sleep experts say one late night is usually fine as long as regular sleep times return soon.

quests.instruction: Before making a shopping list, what should Kemi's family check first?
quests.correctAnswer: What food they already have at home 🥫
options: What food they already have at home 🥫
Which store in town is the biggest 🏬
Who ate the most dinner last week 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about how to avoid buying things you already have.
quests.explanation: Checking cupboards and the fridge first saves money and stops food from going to waste.
quests.funFact: Roughly a third of the food produced around the world is lost or wasted.

quests.instruction: Which plate has the most balanced mix of foods?
quests.correctAnswer: Rice, beans, and vegetables 🍽️
options: A plate with only chips 🍟
Rice, beans, and vegetables 🍽️
A plate with only cake 🍰
quests.hint: A balanced meal has foods from several groups.
quests.explanation: Different foods give the body different nutrients. Grains, protein foods, and vegetables together make a balanced plate.
quests.funFact: Many cultures have traditional balanced meals, such as rice with dal, or tortillas with beans.

quests.instruction: Six people each eat 2 rolls. Rolls are sold in packs of 4. How many packs does the family need?
quests.correctAnswer: 3 packs 🛒
options: 2 packs 🛒
3 packs 🛒
4 packs 🛒
quests.hint: First work out how many rolls are needed in all.
quests.explanation: 6 people × 2 rolls is 12 rolls, and 12 ÷ 4 is 3 packs.
quests.funFact: Working out how many equal packs to buy is something families and shops do every day.

quests.instruction: Isla's family reads quietly in the same room each evening, each with their own book. Is that time together?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, sharing a space can be time together 💛
options: No, because no one is talking 🤫
No, because they have different books 📚
Yes, sharing a space can be time together 💛
quests.hint: Does being together always mean talking?
quests.explanation: Quiet time in the same room can feel close and calm. Togetherness does not always need talking.
quests.funFact: Reading near each other is a popular way to share a quiet evening.

quests.instruction: On Friday movie night, a different family member picks the film each week. Why is that a good idea?
quests.correctAnswer: So everyone gets a turn to choose 🎬
options: So the oldest person always decides 👑
So the film is always very short ⏱️
So everyone gets a turn to choose 🎬
quests.hint: Think about fairness.
quests.explanation: Taking turns makes sure everyone's choice counts over time.
quests.funFact: Many families rotate the choice of movie, meal, or game so that everyone feels heard.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a free family activity?
quests.correctAnswer: Walking to the park together 🌳
options: Buying tickets for a theme park 🎢
Walking to the park together 🌳
Eating out at a restaurant 🍽️
quests.hint: Which activity needs no money at all?
quests.explanation: Walks, board games, and picnics at home cost little or nothing. What matters is the time together, not the money spent.
quests.funFact: Many libraries, parks, and community events are free for families.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a family routine?
quests.correctAnswer: Breakfast together every Saturday 🥞
options: A surprise birthday party for a cousin 🎂
Breakfast together every Saturday 🥞
A trip that happens only one time ✈️
quests.hint: A routine is something that happens again and again.
quests.explanation: Routines are habits repeated on a regular basis, which gives days a pattern. Surprises and one-off events are not routines.
quests.funFact: Studies suggest that regular family routines are linked to children feeling more secure.

quests.instruction: Faye's family has dinner at different times on different days because of work. Which statement is true?
quests.correctAnswer: A routine can change and still work 🔄
options: A routine can change and still work 🔄
That family has no routine at all 🚫
That family is doing something wrong 😟
quests.hint: Do all routines have to look exactly the same?
quests.explanation: Routines can be flexible. A family can have a pattern that shifts with work and school hours.
quests.funFact: Many families build routines around shifts, travel, or sports, and no single pattern is right for everyone.

quests.instruction: Cam's family leaves at 8:15. The drive to school takes 25 minutes, and school starts at 8:45. Will they arrive on time?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, with 5 minutes to spare ✅
options: No, they will be 5 minutes late ⏰
Yes, with 5 minutes to spare ✅
No, they will be 15 minutes late ⏰
quests.hint: Add 25 minutes to 8:15.
quests.explanation: 8:15 plus 25 minutes is 8:40, which is five minutes before school starts.
quests.funFact: Leaving a few minutes early gives a family space for traffic or a forgotten bag.
